name: BattleEffect_RunFallbackObjectTransition

score.note: Improved from a prior draft (448/197/102) by correcting the BattleEffectMotionRecord stride (0x48, not 0x120), hoisting step=0 before the null-object check, and switching the 16-record loop to a descending counter with a walking record pointer -- all three moves match the reference disassembly's own idiom exactly and pulled candidate_bytes to the exact 444-byte target. The remaining 165-halfword residual is concentrated in one region: the compiler's register promotion of the origin/destination interpolation-array base pointers into sl/r8 differs from the reference's choice (which pointer gets sl vs r8), which cascades through the whole interpolation loop and the trailing loop-bound comparison (cmp #10/ble vs cmp #11/blt). Six declaration-order and expression-shape respellings were tried against this one region; none reproduced the reference's exact sl/r8 binding without cost elsewhere, so this is recorded as a genuine register-allocator sensitivity rather than a semantic gap.

rejected_experiments: Locals declared position,origin,destination (top-to-bottom) does yield the reference's correct stack offsets (origin@sp+12, destination@sp+0, position@sp+24) but costs 4 extra bytes (448) from a different sl/r8 promotion order -- worse net score (448/174/90) than the accepted origin,destination,position order despite the offsets being individually 'more correct'.

Explicit origin_ptr/destination_ptr local pointer variables in place of array-literal indexing: 456/222/150, substantially worse -- the compiler synthesizes its own base-pointer temporaries more efficiently than an explicit alias.
Splitting object->z into a temporary (z) plus a separate delta temporary to try to reproduce the reference's delayed str r5,[r6,#16] scheduling around the scale calc: 456/207/98, worse.
Locals declared destination,position,origin (top-to-bottom): 448/176/94, worse than accepted order.
Locals declared destination,origin,position (top-to-bottom): 448/? not adopted -- superseded by testing the full permutation set; origin,destination,position remained best throughout.
notes: Recovered only from the retained owner assembly, approved local ROM, the byte-exact template/sibling sources, in-repository headers, and the approved compiler.
This candidate claims zero DONE bytes.

Complete typed fallback path for battle effect 9. It interpolates a temporary object from the selected target toward the battle origin over 11 steps, runs a timed sound sequence, spawns sixteen motion records (0x48-byte stride, not the 0x120 previously assumed) walking forward from state->records[0] while a separate index counts 15 downto 0, then releases the temporary object after fixed delays.

The exact-C dispatcher enters exact 0809ab98 only when target-object setup fails; 0809ab98 marks the active object and immediately calls this owner. The three-owner producer/consumer chain covers 808 executable bytes (see prior dossier revision for exact_c_dispatcher/setup addresses).

Independent relocation-aware matching (from the prior dossier revision) proved 320 normalized core bytes identical at unique JA/EN/DE/ES/FR/IT anchors; that analysis was not re-verified in this pass but nothing in this revision's struct-layout correction should affect it, since it only changed local variable placement and loop shape, not the cross-edition call/literal skeleton.

No GS2 or external source was used; the orbiting_particles/run.c family hint was read in full but its loop shape (random per-particle spawn over 15 iterations) does not structurally match this owner's single-object interpolation + fixed 16-record spawn, so it was not used as a direct structural template -- only its general battle-effect idiom (Data_03001f30 scene pointer, WaitFrames/Audio_PlayCue-style helper calls) informed variable naming conventions already present in the prior draft.
